section_1.title: Prerequisite Review: The Two Pillars
section_1.content: Briefly visualize differentiation as finding the 'instantaneous slope' (the speed of a racing cheetah) and integration as finding the 'accumulated area' (total distance traveled by the cheetah). Establish the mindset that these seem like opposites.
section_1.example: Animation: A cheetah running. The derivative captures the speedometer reading at time t; the integral captures the total territory covered.

section_2.title: Visualizing the Inverse Relationship
section_2.content: Introduce the 'Accumulation Function' F(x) = ∫ f(t)dt. Show a dynamic graph where moving the upper limit 'x' sweeps out an area. Demonstrate that as 'x' grows by a tiny increment, the new sliver of area added is roughly the height of the function, suggesting the derivative of the area is the function itself.
section_2.example: Animation: An expanding rectangle under a curve. As the right edge slides, the growth rate of the shaded area perfectly matches the function's height f(x).

section_3.title: The Fundamental Theorem (Part 1)
section_3.content: Formalize the relationship: The derivative of the integral of a function is the original function. Explain this as the 'undoing' of accumulation. Emphasize that differentiation and integration are inverse operations.
section_3.example: A 'magic machine': Input a function f(x) -> Integrate it (accumulate) -> Differentiate the result -> You get back f(x).

section_4.title: The Fundamental Theorem (Part 2) & Application
section_4.content: Introduce the evaluation tool: ∫[a to b] f(x)dx = F(b) - F(a), where F is the antiderivative. This bridges the gap between geometry and algebra, allowing us to calculate area without counting infinite tiny rectangles.
section_4.example: Example: Calculate the area under f(x) = 2x from 0 to 3. We show the integral calculation resulting in 9, and verify it with the geometric area of a triangle (Base 3, Height 6, Area = 0.5 * 3 * 6 = 9).

section_5.title: Summary & Synthesis
section_5.content: Recap: We started with two seemingly unrelated problems (slope vs. area) and unified them. The theorem turns the hard task of summing infinite slivers into the simpler task of finding an antiderivative.
section_5.example: A conceptual map showing a path from 'Area summation' to 'Antiderivative calculation' connected by the Fundamental Theorem.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
